text:
sophie: Quick heads-up — planning a 2hr maintenance quiet window for eu-west1 this Saturday 02:00-04:00 UTC. Scope: BMC/fan firmware rollout on 3 racks + linux kernel micropatch. This will be rolling (node-by-node), not whole-pool down. Please read plan and shout if you have blockers.

mike: ack. can you paste the drain strategy? need to confirm we won't tear down long-running fine-tunes mid-epoch.

sophie: plan is: cordon -> annotate job for graceful eviction -> 30m drain timeout -> migrate remaining short tasks. Long-running jobs with label `non-preempt=true` are exempt. we'll set `evictionGracePeriod=30m`.

sophie: k8s snippet:```kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=1800```

raj: if we proactively backfill to us-west for hot capacity, what's the cost delta? I want a rough number to justify to finance.

lee: cross-region backfill adds network egress + spot GPU costs. rough calc: ~10 GPUs * $0.80/hr (spot) + egress ~ $0.20/hr => ~ $10/hr. but if we need burst to 40 GPUs it's closer to $40/hr. also watch latency-sensitive hosted routes.

mike: from infra side: prefer to avoid wide cross-region reroutes for the whole 2hr window. propose a mixed approach: 50% local backfill from spare warm pools + 50% limited us-west burst for priority tenants. reduces risk and cost.

sophie: agree. i'll mark priority tenants in the maint ticket and add a fallback policy: if latency > 200ms for 5m, route to us-west pool.

lee: put a temporary SLO relax rule for the oncall runbooks so we don't get noisy pages for transient spikes during the window. oncall-bot, can you add that?

oncall-bot: created INC-2024-9985 and updated paging config: `slo_latency_threshold=250ms` for maintenance window. link: https://infra.redwood/internal/inc/INC-2024-9985

raj: customer comms — do we send a notice? it's rolling but some dedicated customers might want heads-up. we should email only enterprise customers with reserved capacity.

sophie: yes — Customer Success draft: short bullet email explaining rolling hardware firmware, expected minimal interruption, recommended that teams avoid launching new long-running experiments during 02:00-06:00 UTC (we add 2hr buffer). i'll post draft in #customer-success for review.

mike: two safety asks: 1) prefix KV cache warm-up after each node comes back (so latency doesn't spike for first requests), 2) ensure automatic fallback model variant is enabled for small-tier tenants.

sophie: good call. we'll run `prefix-cache-warmup` job per rack:```for node in $RACK_NODES; do ssh $node 'curl https://warmup.redwood/prefix?list=top50' & done```

lee: ops checklist: preflight health checks 24h prior, 1h prior noise test, run canary on 2 nodes, then ramp. Can we add a post-maint metric check to auto-rollback if token latency 95p increases >30%?

sophie: yes. I'll add a rollback trigger: if 95p tokens > baseline*1.3 for 10m -> stop rollout and reinstate previous kernel. documented in the ticket.

mike: who will own the live run? I can be primary, raj can do routing, lee on call. sophie owns comms and rollback. pls confirm.

sophie: assigned: mike (lead), raj (routing/fallback), lee (oncall/monitoring), sophie (owner & comms).

raj: one more: we should mark capacity as billable in the cost center `infra-maint-2024` so finance can track burst spend.

sophie: done. put a note in the ticket with estimated spend upper bound $600.

lee: I'll post a quick #eng-sre alert 15m before start and pin the playbook. Add emoji reactions for ack.

mike: :thumbsup:

sophie: thanks all. I'll push the maintenance ticket and the customer email draft by EOD. If no objections by 18:00 UTC today we'll lock the window.

raj: ack.

lee: ack.

mike: ack.

sophie: closing out here — final note: keep an eye on persistent volumes during drain; we've seen one PV detach flake before. I'll add a PV sanity check to preflight.
